newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes Russia, NATO new partnership pact.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes Russia, NATO new partnership pact.

text.p: China on Thursday issued a cautious welcome to Russia and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) forging a peaceful new relationship, saying it was conducive to world peace.

"We are willing to see Russia further improve its relations with other European countries and develop their relations," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said when asked to comment on the agreement.
"We hope the pact will help safeguard security and the interests of all sides in this region and is also conducive to peace and stability in Europe and the whole world," Shen told a news briefing.

Russia and NATO held talks in Moscow and issued a joint statement on Wednesday saying the former Cold War enemies had made "decisive progress" on key issues including military issues, which had been the main obstacles to agreement.
The agreement is intended to placate Russia before NATO invites new members from eastern Europe. Russian leaders have spoken out strongly against NATO expansion, calling it a threat to its security.

The agreement cleared the way for Russia's President Boris Yeltsin and NATO to sign the deal in Paris on May 27, providing the text is approved by the Kremlin leader and the heads of government of the 16 NATO countries.
